hub.funnelBody:
Bank Strongholds follow the same lifecycle every time:

1. Battle planning — mark the target on Battle Plan before you capture it.
2. Create the bank — register it in Bank Management, either from a City List screenshot or by hand.
3. Record a deposit video — capture Bank Info, optional Favorites, and Deposit Slip History in one upload.
4. Review and commit — confirm the bank and deposit rows, then submit.
5. Ongoing operations — track active, elapsed, matured, and looted deposits, stats, and risk as the bank runs.
6. Abandon and drop — stop new deposits, wait for maturity, and schedule the in-game drop.

Each step below links to full instructions.

abandonDrop.instructions:
When a bank is nearing the end of its life:

1. Stop new deposits — tell investors to stop depositing (or tighten the deposit policy) once you're planning to abandon it, so no one locks in a fresh term right before you drop.
2. Wait for maturity — use the Investor risk heatmap and falloff projection to find a time when as many deposits as possible have matured, minimizing value at risk.
3. Set the drop deadline — edit the bank and set Need to drop by to the date/time you must abandon it in-game (for example, when the stronghold's protection expires). This date drives the Past drop deadline section.
4. Schedule the drop — from the Recommended next drop card, click Schedule drop to add a Bank drop event to Battle Plan at the recommended (or a custom) time, so members see the announcement and know to limit new deposit terms.

Once a bank's Need to drop by time passes, it moves into the Past drop deadline section of Bank Strongholds — still tracked in HQ, but flagged so you can confirm whether it's still held in-game or has already been dropped.
abandonDrop.summary: Stop taking new deposits, wait for terms to mature, set the drop deadline, and schedule the in-game drop.
abandonDrop.tip: Setting Need to drop by as soon as you capture a bank, even a rough estimate, keeps it from landing in Past drop deadline by surprise later, and keeps the drop recommendation accurate.
abandonDrop.title: Abandon the bank and schedule the drop

battlePlanning.instructions:
Open Battle Plan and schedule a capture for the stronghold (or city) you're about to take.

• Set the territory type and, if you've already scouted it, the target coordinates — Battle Plan can auto-create a matching Bank in Bank Management once you confirm the capture later.
• Add a marker so members know which target you mean, and announce it to the alliance straight from Battle Plan.
• Capturing without pre-scouted coordinates is fine too — add the Bank by hand once you hold it (see the next step).

Already hold the stronghold? Battle planning is optional — skip straight to creating the bank.
battlePlanning.summary: Mark the stronghold or city you're about to take, with target coordinates, before you touch Bank Management.
battlePlanning.title: Plan the capture in Battle Plan

createBanks.instructions:
Open Bank Management and add the stronghold as a Bank. Two ways in:

1. City List import (fastest for many banks) — click Import banks from screenshot and upload one or more in-game City List → Bank Stronghold screenshots. HQ reads server, coordinates, level, and current deposit value/count from each row and merges duplicates by coordinates. Capture overlapping shots if you hold more banks than fit on one screen.
2. Manual entry — click Add bank and enter the server, X/Y coordinates, and Stronghold level yourself. Use this for a single new capture, or when an import missed one.

Either way, the bank now appears in your Bank Strongholds list, where you can set its deposit policy (alliance members, same warzone, or public).
createBanks.summary: Once you hold the stronghold, register it as a Bank — import from a City List screenshot, or add it by hand.
createBanks.tip: No screenshot handy? Capture Bank Info and Favorites frames in the deposit video from the next step instead — HQ can use those to help align coordinates to the right bank.
createBanks.title: Create the bank in Bank Management

ongoingOps.instructions:
Once a bank has deposit slips, Bank Management gives you the tools to run it day to day:

• Filters — switch between Active (Deposited, still earning), Elapsed (term passed but not yet matured in-game), Matured, and Looted to see exactly where each deposit stands.
• Stats — Total deposited, Recovered, Lost to looting, and Interest earned (once you've imported deposit slip history) summarize the bank's performance at a glance.
• Investor risk heatmap — shows which of the next 72 hours have the fewest Deposited deposits at risk, so you know when it's safest to drop.
• Deposit falloff projection — projects deposited value and maturity outflow over time; save a snapshot to compare against what actually happens.
• Recommended next drop — HQ highlights the lowest-level bank with the least value at risk as your best drop candidate.

Check in regularly — new deposits, maturing deposits, and shifting risk change the recommendation as time passes.

recordDepositVideo.instructions:
From the Bank Stronghold in-game, record a single video that walks through:

1. Bank Info — open the bank's info panel so HQ can read its level, owning alliance tag, current deposit value, and deposit capacity.
2. Favorites (optional, but recommended) — if the bank is starred in your Favorites list, open that screen too. Favorites shows exact X/Y coordinates, which HQ trusts over other sources when aligning the bank.
3. Deposit Slip History — scroll all the way through your deposit slip history so every Deposited, Matured, and Looted deposit is on screen.

Upload the video from Tools → Video upload, or tap the video icon next to a bank in Bank Management to jump straight to upload with that bank pre-selected.

HQ's OCR reads all three frame types from the same video: Bank Info and Favorites feed the bank's context (coordinates, level, alliance tag, deposit value), while Deposit Slip History becomes the individual deposit rows you'll review next.
recordDepositVideo.summary: One video: open Bank Info, optionally swing by Favorites for exact coordinates, then scroll Deposit Slip History — HQ reads all three.
recordDepositVideo.tip: Recording Bank Info and Favorites before you scroll deposit history gives HQ the best chance to align coordinates ahead of review — but the order doesn't have to be exact.
recordDepositVideo.title: Record and upload the deposit video

reviewAndCommit.instructions:
After processing, open the review page for your upload:

1. Confirm the Bank selector matches the stronghold you recorded — HQ pre-selects your most recently used bank, so double-check it, especially if you've uploaded more than one bank's video recently.
2. Walk each parsed deposit slip row: term, amount, status (Deposited/Matured/Looted), and commander name. Fix anything the OCR misread — you can preview the source video frame for any row.
3. Submit once everything looks right. Committed slips merge into that bank's deposit list, and duplicates from re-uploads are deduped automatically.

If a bank's coordinates look wrong, correct them in Bank Management before you submit so future uploads keep aligning cleanly.

privacy.encryptionIntro: When you connect Alliance HQ to ashed.online, you paste a network request that contains a login token (JWT). That token is the key that lets Alliance HQ talk to Ashed as you. We treat it like a password.

encryptionSteps.disconnect: You can disconnect. Settings → Disconnect removes your stored connection key from our server.
encryptionSteps.encrypted: Encrypted before storage. As soon as we receive your token, we encrypt it with AES-256-GCM (industry-standard authenticated encryption) before writing anything to our database.
encryptionSteps.separateKey: Separate encryption key. The key used to encrypt your token lives only in our server environment — it is never stored in the database alongside your encrypted token, and it is never sent to your browser.
encryptionSteps.serverSide: Server-side only. Your browser receives a short-lived session cookie. The Ashed JWT itself stays on our server and is decrypted only when Alliance HQ needs to call Ashed for you.
encryptionSteps.uniqueIv: Unique ciphertext each time. Each encryption uses a fresh random value (IV), so even identical tokens would not produce identical stored data.

privacy.encryptionTitle: How your Ashed connection key is protected
privacy.intro: Alliance HQ at frontline.gay is a community tool for Last War alliance officers. This page explains what we store and how we protect it.
privacy.noSellBody1: Alliance HQ exists to help your alliance use ashed.online more easily. We will never sell, rent, or trade your personal information or alliance data to third parties. We do not use your data for advertising, and we do not build marketing profiles from your activity.
privacy.noSellBody2: We only use the information needed to run the service you asked for — for example, keeping you signed in and calling Ashed on your behalf when you use Alliance HQ features.
privacy.noSellTitle: We do not sell your data
privacy.questionsBody: This policy may be updated as Alliance HQ grows. If you have questions about your data, open an issue on our <githubLink>GitHub repository</githubLink>.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.whatWeStoreFooter: Alliance reports, member lists, and other alliance content stay on Ashed's systems. Alliance HQ does not copy that data into a separate database for resale or unrelated purposes.

whatWeStoreItems.label: An optional display label (for example, your Ashed account name) so we can show who is connected.
whatWeStoreItems.metadata: Basic connection metadata, such as when your token expires and your reminder preferences.
whatWeStoreItems.session: A random session identifier in an httpOnly cookie in your browser (not your Ashed login token).
whatWeStoreItems.token: Your Ashed connection key (JWT), encrypted on our server — see below.

privacy.whereDataBody: Alliance HQ runs on managed cloud hosting (Vercel for the app, Neon Postgres for encrypted credentials and session data). Data is transmitted over HTTPS.

walkthrough.step1: This is your train scheduling hub. Train days follow game server time (UTC−2). The badge above always shows the current server date and time — use it when planning rolls and locks. If you lock a conductor, you can unlock it until midnight Server Time of that train day.
walkthrough.step10: All your past conductors, VIPs, and what rules won them the train are searchable here.
walkthrough.step11: You can adjust your preferred start of week, score and donation minimums, Discord announcements and more in the Settings menu.
walkthrough.step12: That's it! Please enjoy, and take a moment to leave us feedback.
walkthrough.step2: You can set the conductor and VIP rules for a whole week. Try changing this week's train to Economy Week (R3 Lottery) — changes won't take effect while this tour is active.
walkthrough.step3: Great! Now let's change the rules for today's train. Press and hold today's tile, and then choose a different rule from the menu.
walkthrough.step4: This is where you set up the day's Conductor and VIP. You can do this for the current day, or for any future day.
walkthrough.step5: The Conductor step is where you draw the conductor. If a prerequisite, like VS scores or donations, is missing, you'll upload those as part of the Conductor flow.
walkthrough.step6: Random walk pools get depleted as each member gets their turn for Conductor. You can check who is left in the current pool by clicking here.
walkthrough.step7: Easily plan out a whole week's worth of conductors with one tap. Give it a try!
walkthrough.step8: Now let's switch to Month view for longer term planning.
walkthrough.step9: Select days on the calendar, then pick a rule from the palette to paint them. Tap or drag on mobile; click, drag, or Shift+click a range on desktop.
